title: India Waives $25 OCI Passport-Update Penalty Until December 31, 2026
excerpt: It is a one-time waiver, not a removal: late updates received between November 1 and December 31 escape the $25 penalty, which returns on January 1, 2027.
body:
• India has waived the $25 penalty for late OCI passport updates for a one-time window: updates received from November 1 to December 31, 2026.
  • The underlying rule has not changed — OCI holders must update new passport details within 3 months of receiving a new passport, or the $25 penalty applies; it returns on January 1, 2027.
  • The waiver does not cover updates submitted before November 1, and other OCI fees — including $25 for changes of personal particulars — still apply.
  • OCI holders can travel to and from India while a delayed passport update is under process, the government has clarified.

If you hold an Overseas Citizen of India card and renewed your foreign passport more than three months ago without updating the OCI portal, India is giving you until the end of the year to fix it free. The Government of India has waived the $25 late fee for OCI cardholders with delayed passport updates, in what Indian Eagle's report describes as a one-time relief for two months, from November 1 to December 31, 2026. A UK notice summarised by Matrix Solutions confirms the waiver applies to all OCI cards, whichever Indian mission issued them.

Who is affected — and who is not

The 2026 OCI rules require cardholders to update their passport details on the OCI portal within three months of receiving a new passport, every time, with a $25 penalty for missing the deadline. The waiver covers exactly that penalty, for updates received inside the November-December window — including passports renewed long before the window opened. It does not cover late applications submitted before November 1, 2026, which are not eligible. And it should not be mistaken for a wider fee holiday: fees for other OCI services, including duplicate card issuance, renunciation, reissuance after the age of 20, and the $25 charge for changing personal particulars such as name or nationality, continue to apply. Background on the current fee bands and the e-OCI system is in VisaVerge's 2026 OCI guide.

What to do, and by when

File the update through the e-OCI portal before December 31, 2026. There is no certainty of an extension: late update applications resume attracting the $25 fee from January 1, 2027. In the UK, VFS has said OCI Miscellaneous updates are processed without a VFS visit, according to the notice summarised by Matrix. One reassurance for anyone mid-process during the holiday travel season: the Government of India has clarified that OCI cardholders can travel to and from India even if they delayed updating new passport details, with no travel restrictions while the update application is under process.

The wider 2026 OCI overhaul behind the rule

The three-month update rule arrived with a broader rebuild of the OCI system this year. The Ministry of Home Affairs moved OCI registration fully online through the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026, published in the Gazette on April 30, and Home Minister Amit Shah launched the electronic e-OCI card in New Delhi on June 30, according to VisaVerge's guide. For applicants in the United States, a new OCI registration costs $275 in government fees, plus a $3 Indian Community Welfare Fund charge and a $19 VFS Global service fee. The same overhaul ended the old requirement to obtain a fresh OCI booklet after a new passport issued past age 20; an online update is now sufficient in most cases, which is exactly the step the waiver makes free until December 31.

Why this window exists

The waiver lands at the start of the busiest India travel season of the year, when large numbers of diaspora families fly in for Diwali and the winter holidays — precisely the moment an out-of-date OCI record surfaces at a check-in desk. The three-month update rule itself is recent, part of the 2026 tightening of OCI compliance that also standardised the $275 fresh application fee. The waiver is best read as a grace period for that new rule: file by New Year's Eve and the overdue update costs nothing.
